package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical vulnerability (SpringShell, CVE-2022-22965) that allows remote code execution under certain conditions. While not intentionally malicious, its presence in a project can enable attackers to exploit systems if not properly mitigated or updated.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code allows manipulation of the class loader via crafted HTTP requests, enabling attackers to set arbitrary fields on Java objects, which can lead to remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The ability to set arbitrary fields on Java objects via HTTP requests is highly abnormal and dangerous, as it can be leveraged to achieve remote code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal web controllers should not expose internal class loader or object field manipulation to external users. This behavior breaks encapsulation and security boundaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of @InitBinder is to customize data binding in Spring MVC, but not to allow unrestricted field access.
key_indicators: Exposes internal object fields to external manipulation
Allows setting of class loader properties via HTTP
Can be triggered remotely with crafted requests

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP request to a vulnerable endpoint in a Spring MVC application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary field manipulation on Java objects within the application context.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable code allows the attacker to set properties that control the class loader.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the server.

behavioral_signatures: HTTP requests attempting to set class loader or internal Java object fields
Unusual use of @InitBinder with broad or wildcard field access
Runtime manipulation of object fields via web endpoints
file_indicators: Presence of vulnerable versions of org.springframework:spring-webmvc JARs
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with parameters targeting class loader or internal fields
Unusual POST/PUT requests to endpoints accepting Java Beans
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for HTTP requests attempting to set fields such as 'class.*' or 'Class.*' in Spring MVC endpoints. Scan for vulnerable versions of org.springframework:spring-webmvc in dependencies. Review @InitBinder methods for overly permissive field access. Use runtime instrumentation to detect attempts to manipulate class loader properties via web requests.
